title: The Lesion That Needed a Name — Dermatopathologic & Autopsy Differentiation of Benign Vascular/Cutaneous Mimics From Abuse or Fatal Systemic Vasculopathy

teenKit.tldr: A forensic case study reveals that a localized skin cancer doesn't always need to spread to other organs to kill a person; sheer local tissue destruction can trigger a fatal systemic crash.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It shatters the common myth that skin issues are purely cosmetic or safe as long as they stay in one place, proving that early attention can literally save your life.
keyTakeaways: Cancer can be deadly purely through local scale and destruction, without ever needing to metastasize or travel to the lungs or liver.
The human body can visibly display massive medical emergencies right on the surface, yet people can still dangerously delay getting help.
Forensic pathology and autopsies act like scientific detective work, separating actual biological facts from assumptions about how a person died.

vocab.meaning: The specialized study and diagnosis of skin diseases at a microscopic level.
The process where cancer cells break away from the original tumor and travel to other parts of the body.
A destructive disease affecting blood vessels throughout the entire body system.
A thorough surgical examination of a body after death to determine the exact cause and manner of dying.

quiz.question: According to the episode, what major assumption about cancer does this case shatter?
options: That cancer can only be cured with surgery
That cancer is only fatal when it spreads to distant organs like the lungs or liver
That skin cancer only happens to older adults
That tumors cannot grow on the human scalp
